Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: the request needs an account and carries no valid token.

country.description: The pilot's own country, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, if they set one. Left out while it is not set.

edits_sites.description: True for an account whoever runs the server named as one of Venti's partners for flying sites; left out for every other.

google_email.description: The email of the Google account the account is signed in to with, if it is linked to one. Only in the account's own answers.

new_flights_public.description: Whether a flight the pilot uploads is public from the start: the pilot's own setting, on until they switch it off. A suspended account's uploads are private whatever it says. Left out by a server from before the setting, which made new flights private.

picture.description: The path of the account's picture, if it has one: GET /v1/pictures/{id}.

shown_near_places.description: Whether the pilot is among the pilots near a place (GET /v1/pilots/near): the pilot's own setting, on until they switch it off. Left out by a server from before the setting, which had no such list.

AircraftKind.description: What kind of aircraft another network says a position is of. A word this version does not know is to be read as `unknown`.

name.description: What the pilot calls the alarm: 1 to 60 characters.

AlertRule.description: What an alarm waits for, told apart by `kind`: `wind`, `day` or `pilots`. A kind a client does not know is left as it is.

agree.description: true to agree, false to refuse.

Attribution.description: The credit of one data source an answer draws on. Whoever shows the data shows `text`, linked to `url`, next to it, and `notice` if there is one: the sources' licences require it. An answer's `attributions` has one entry per source it draws on, and only those.

redirect_to.description: The program's own address, as it registered it, with the code or the refusal, the program's state, and iss. The browser is sent there.

lasts.description: For how long the agreement holds, in the server's words.

may_not.description: What it may not do, in the server's words.

may_read.description: What the program may read once the pilot agrees, in the server's words: one sentence for each thing.

on_this_device.description: Whether that address is a program on the device the browser runs on.

program.description: What the program calls itself: its own claim, which nobody checked.

returns_to.description: The host the pilot's browser is sent back to with the answer.

Cable.description: One cable hung in the air, of exactly one source, as a line. A height is given only where the source maps one; no cable in an answer is no statement that there is none.

cheers.description: How many pilots cheer the flight now.

cheered.description: Whether the account that asks cheered the flight. Absent when nobody is signed in.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

text.description: Plain text of at most 500 characters. Show it as text, never as markup.
Plain text; at most 500 characters once trimmed.

count.description: How many comments the flight has now.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

open.description: False once the flight's pilot turned comments off; those written before stay.

ConfirmSiteRequest.description: "I took off here and it was good": the day, a line if wanted, and one of the pilot's own flights if wanted, by its address.

google_id_token.description: A fresh Google ID token of the linked Google account, in place of the password.

DeviceRequest.description: A phone's token from its platform's push service.

sandbox.description: An iPhone app built for development, whose token is of Apple's sandbox. Left out for every other.

token.description: On an iPhone the device token in hexadecimal; on Android the FCM registration token. At most 512 bytes.

DumpContent.description: What a file of a dump holds: the sites of a layer as they stand, or every site the layer ever had with every revision.

DumpFile.description: One file of a layer's dump. `bytes` and `sha256` are of the file before any compression on the way.

DumpFormat.description: The format of a file of a dump: GeoJSON, CSV, or JSON Lines.

ErrorCode.description: A stable code. `x-venti-values` lists the codes the server has today; docs/api.md says which status each comes with and when. A client must expect codes it does not know.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every answer with a 4xx or 5xx status.

info.description:
Made by the server from its own table of routes and held to it by tests. docs/api.md in the repository says in words what every field means, when each error comes and what the bounds are; `x-venti-docs` on an operation names its heading there, and "Writing a program against Venti" is where to begin.

Within `/v1` the format only grows: an answer may gain fields and a list of known values may gain entries, so a client ignores what it does not know. No schema here closes a record against further fields. Where a schema has `x-venti-values`, those are the values there are today, and others may come.

A value that is not known is left out of an answer: a field is never null. Null stands only inside a list with an entry per cell of the thermal map's grid, for a cell without a value; its schema says so.

The data of others is handed out under its sources' licences: every answer that carries such data names them in `attributions`, and answers with flights of pilots carry `terms`.
